content:
**Step 1.  Factor the given number**

\[
17017 = 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
17017^{17}=7^{17}\,11^{17}\,13^{17}\,17^{17}.
\]

A divisor of \(17017^{17}\) has the form  

\[
d=7^{a}\,11^{b}\,13^{c}\,17^{d},\qquad
0\le a,b,c,d\le 17 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 2.  Work modulo \(12\).**  

Since \(7,11,13,17\) are all odd and not divisible by \(3\),

\[
7\equiv7\pmod{12},\quad 
11\equiv -1\pmod{12},\quad 
13\equiv 1\pmod{12},\quad 
17\equiv 5\pmod{12}.
\]

The orders of these residues are all \(2\):
\[
7^2\equiv1,\;11^2\equiv1,\;5^2\equiv1\pmod{12}.
\]

Thus only the *parities* of the exponents matter:

\[
7^{a}\equiv\begin{cases}
1 & a\text{ even}\\[2pt]
7 & a\text{ odd}
\end{cases},\qquad
11^{b}\equiv\begin{cases}
1 & b\text{ even}\\[2pt]
11 & b\text{ odd}
\end{cases},\qquad
17^{d}\equiv\begin{cases}
1 & d\text{ even}\\[2pt]
5 & d\text{ odd}
\end{cases}.
\]

The factor \(13^{c}\equiv1\) never changes the residue, so we may ignore \(c\) for the congruence condition.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 3.  Find the parity patterns that give residue \(5\).**

Compute the product \(7^{a}11^{b}5^{d}\) for all \(2^3=8\) parity combinations:

| \(a\) (parity) | \(b\) (parity) | \(d\) (parity) | Product mod 12 |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| even           | even           | even           | 1 |
| even           | even           | odd            | **5** |
| even           | odd            | even           | 11 |
| even           | odd            | odd            | 7 |
| odd            | even           | even           | 7 |
| odd            | even           | odd            | 11 |
| odd            | odd            | even           | **5** |
| odd            | odd            | odd            | 1 |

The product is \(5\) for exactly two patterns:

* **(A)** \(a\) even, \(b\) even, \(d\) odd;
* **(B)** \(a\) odd,  \(b\) odd,  \(d\) even.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 4.  Count the exponent choices.**

Each exponent ranges from \(0\) to \(17\) inclusive, giving \(18\) possibilities.
Among these, there are \(9\) even numbers and \(9\) odd numbers.

*Pattern (A)*:  
\(a\) even \(\rightarrow 9\) choices,  
\(b\) even \(\rightarrow 9\) choices,  
\(d\) odd  \(\rightarrow 9\) choices.  

Hence \(9^3 = 729\) triples \((a,b,d)\).

*Pattern (B)*:  
\(a\) odd \(\rightarrow 9\) choices,  
\(b\) odd \(\rightarrow 9\) choices,  
\(d\) even \(\rightarrow 9\) choices.  

Again \(9^3 = 729\) triples.

So the number of \((a,b,d)\) satisfying the congruence is  

\[
729+729 = 1458.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 5.  Include the exponent of \(13\).**

The exponent \(c\) of the factor \(13^{c}\) is unrestricted: it can be any of the \(18\) values \(0,\dots,17\).  
Thus each admissible \((a,b,d)\) yields \(18\) possible divisors.

\[
N = 1458 \times 18 = 26244.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 6.  Reduce modulo \(1000\).**

\[
26244 \equiv 244 \pmod{1000}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

\[
\boxed{244}
\]
